---
title: "Getting started"
---

You need about 20 minutes and a phone for this, once.

## 1. Create a Kaggle account

[Kaggle](https://www.kaggle.com) gives everyone free GPU time in the browser. It is the main platform for this course.

1. Sign up at [kaggle.com](https://www.kaggle.com).
2. Go to **Settings → Phone verification** and verify your phone number.
   Without this you cannot switch on a GPU or the internet in a notebook, and lessons will not work.
3. Have a look at your weekly GPU quota (about 30 hours, shown in any notebook's right-hand panel). The lessons are designed to use only a small part of it.

## 2. Open a lesson

Every lesson starts with two badges:

- **Open in Kaggle** makes your own copy of the lesson notebook on Kaggle. Use this one.
- **Open in Colab** opens it on Google Colab instead. Use this if Kaggle is unavailable for some reason.

Each lesson tells you at the top whether it needs a GPU and which data to attach.

## 3. Run a notebook

A notebook is a page made of **cells**. Text cells explain; code cells do something. (For more info about what is a notebook:)

- Click inside a code cell and press **Shift+Enter** to run it. The next cell is selected automatically.
- A running cell shows `[*]`; when it finishes, the star turns into a number.
- Always run cells **from top to bottom**. Later cells use what earlier cells created.
- If something gets stuck: **Run → Restart & clear outputs** (Kaggle) or **Runtime → Restart session** (Colab), then start again from the top.
- Your copy is yours. You cannot break the course by changing it :).

## 4. Save and share

On Kaggle, click **Save Version** to store your work with all outputs. Under **Share** you can make a notebook public.
Every homework ends with sharing: publicly posted notebooks become your portfolio.

## 5. Optional pre-work

Lesson 3 teaches just enough Python to read the notebooks. If you like a head start, try the free
[Kaggle Learn Python](https://www.kaggle.com/learn/python) micro-course. It is not needed for lessons 1 and 2.

## Running on your own computer

Possible, but not needed. See `MAINTAINERS.md` in the repository for the local setup used for testing.
